/-!
# Erdős Problem 246

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/246](https://www.erdosproblems.com/246)
- [Bi59] Birch, B. J., *Note on a problem of Erd\H{o}s*. Proc. Cambridge
  Philos. Soc. (1959), 370-373.
- [Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., *On the representation of integers as the sums of
  distinct summands taken from a fixed set*. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960),
  111-124.
- [FaCh17] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *A quantitative form of the
  {E}rd\H{o}s-{B}irch theorem*. Acta Arith. (2017), 301--311.
- [He00b] Hegyv\'{a}ri, N., *On the completeness of an exponential type
  sequence*. Acta Math. Hungar. (2000), 127--135.
- [Yu24] Yu, Wang-Xing, *On the representation of an exponential type sequence*.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen (2024), 253--261.

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos246

/-- The set $\{a^k b^l : k,l \geq 0\}$. -/
def Gamma (a b : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {x | ∃ k l : ℕ, x = a ^ k * b ^ l}

/--
Let $(a,b)=1$. The set $\{a^kb^l: k,l\geq 0\}$ is complete - that is, every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^kb^l$ with $k,l\geq 0$.

We state the nontrivial case $a,b\geq 2$, proved by Birch [Bi59].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos246.lean"]
theorem erdos_246 (a b : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    IsAddComplete (Gamma a b) := by
  sorry

end Erdos246

reformulations.difference: The source's hypothesis is only "Let (a,b)=1". The Lean adds `2 ≤ a` and `2 ≤ b` on top of `Nat.Coprime a b`. The module docstring says so explicitly: "We state the nontrivial case a,b ≥ 2, proved by Birch [Bi59]".
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Taken literally, the source's wording is false in degenerate cases. a = b = 1 is coprime, Gamma 1 1 = {1}, and no integer ≥ 2 is a subset sum; I proved `Nat.Coprime 1 1 ∧ ¬ IsAddComplete (Gamma 1 1)` in a scratch file. More generally, a = 1 leaves only the powers of b, which are complete only when b = 2. The source attributes the result to Birch ('Proved by Birch [Bi59]'). Birch's theorem is for coprime integers p, q greater than 1: the Fang–Chen abstract (Acta Arith. 178, 2017) says 'for any coprime integers p,q greater than 1 ... every integer n > B can be expressed as the sum of distinct terms taken from {p^a q^b | a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0}'. So the Lean states exactly the theorem the source means, with the same set (1 included) and 'eventually every n is a sum of distinct elements'. The only cases it drops where the claim is true are (1,2) and (2,1), which is just binary expansion. The Lean is not equivalent to the literal wording, which is false; it is the necessary domain restriction the source assumes.

review.notes:
No defects found; the findings list is empty. The file has two declarations, `Erdos246.Gamma` and `Erdos246.erdos_246`, and both match the source.

Checks carried out:
(1) Definitions. `Gamma a b = {x | ∃ k l, x = a^k * b^l}` is the source's set. It contains 1, as Birch's set does. `IsAddComplete` is `∀ᶠ k in atTop, k ∈ subsetSums A`, and a subset sum is the sum of a `Finset` contained in A. That is literally "every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form a^k b^l". Because the summands are distinct integers, there is no multiplicity issue either way. For coprime a, b ≥ 2 the representation a^k b^l is unique in any case.
(2) Status. The file has `research solved` with `formal_proof using lean4`. erdosproblems.com shows 'PROVED (LEAN)' and the teorth data file shows 'proved (Lean)'. These agree.
(3) The `formal_proof` claim. The linked plby/lean-proofs v4.29.1 file and its v4.33.0 'latest' counterpart have identical definitions and statements. They prove `Set.Finite {n | n ∉ FS (Gamma a b)}` under `2 ≤ a`, `2 ≤ b`, `Nat.Coprime a b`. I compiled the latest version against this checkout's Mathlib (v4.33.1) with no errors; `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. In the same file I derived `IsAddComplete (Erdos246.Gamma a b)` under this file's exact hypotheses, using `Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop`. This file's statement is therefore formally proved, which is consistent with its solved status. The proof is about 1100 lines of real mathematics following Birch's argument, so this is not a definitional triviality.
(4) Boundary case. I proved in Lean that the literal hypothesis "(a,b)=1" alone is insufficient: a = b = 1 gives ¬IsAddComplete. The `2 ≤ a`, `2 ≤ b` restriction is therefore required, and it matches Birch's hypotheses. It is recorded as a reformulation above, not as a finding.
(5) Docstrings and references. The main docstring reproduces the erdosproblems.com statement word for word. The references match the site's bibliography and Crossref.

Not formalized, which is an omission and not a defect: the source's remarks give strengthenings that the maintainers could add as variants. These are Davenport's observation that l ≪_{a,b} 1 suffices (quantified by Hegyvári and by Fang–Chen), and Yu's result that all summands can be taken > n/(log n)^{1+o(1)}.

I did not read Birch's 1959 paper itself (paywalled). Its theorem is quoted precisely in the Fang–Chen abstract, so this does not leave anything unsettled. I did not read the erdosproblems.com forum thread, because it may discuss this repository's formalization.
